question: is multi-tool near-mastered or failing outright?
finding: Multi-tool is not failing: 53/73 = 72.6% of multi prompts are answered correctly on all 8 samples, against 16/27 = 59.3% for single. But multi is also wrong outright more often (13.7% vs 11.1% zero-correct), so the pair-producing middle band is much thinner for multi (13.7%) than single (29.6%). That is why y_multi 0.137 is less than half y_single 0.296. Multi's lower yield is a bimodality effect, not a competence deficit.
planning_inference_not_measurement: The frozen weights make multi 73% of every sample, so calibration will be dominated by the stratum with the thinner middle band. On that basis one would EXPECT calibration y_std nearer the pilot's 0.180 than y_single's 0.296. This is an inference from a 100-prompt pilot, not a measurement; only the committed calibration artifact settles it.
